caption: Figure 1: The overview of DChannel. It has two main com- ponents: packet steerer that steers application traffic to LLC and HBC, and reordering buffer that reorders packets coming from LLC.

templates.why_chosen: High-confidence nested-stack exemplar across a five-zone swimlane: the DChannel client box nests a Packet steerer and a Reordering buffer, and the mirrored DChannel proxy box nests the identical pair, tied by two colour-coded channel arrows.
templates.what_to_learn: Nest the same two named sub-modules inside both a client and its mirrored server box so the symmetry is legible from shape alone, then colour-code the parallel channel arrows between them; the weakness here notes those channel colours need a legend, so add one even for two lines.

templates.why_chosen: Five zone columns (User equipment to Base station to Core network to Gateway to Internet) frame a mirrored client/proxy pair, with HBC and LLC drawn as two distinctly coloured dashed paths crossing the same boundaries.
templates.what_to_learn: Draw the network path itself as a series of thin vertical zone columns behind the two mirrored endpoint boxes, and give each of the two parallel channels its own consistent colour end to end; add a small legend naming HBC and LLC, since this figure leaves those abbreviations uncoded.

templates.why_chosen: Ranked first among mirrored-pair exemplars: client and proxy DChannel agents sit at the ends of five network swimlanes, each holding the same Packet steerer/Reordering buffer pair, mirrored in order, around the two crossing HBC/LLC channels.
templates.what_to_learn: Place the mirrored pair at the two ends of a swimlane network path rather than side by side, reverse the internal stacking order on the far side (steerer-then-buffer becomes buffer-then-steerer) to mirror it visually, and label the two crossing channel arrows in the figure itself, since no legend explains HBC and LLC here.
